Great Idea but does not work. The Keurig brewer I just bought does an adequate cup of coffee but the strength is mild to weak. When I saw this product in the brochure inserted with the brewer I was excited this would fix things. I completely filled the filter to the top (just under 3 tablespoons) and found the strength to be identical to coffee made using a pod. I followed the instructions on the grind and had clouds in the coffee so I know I had the grind as fine as possible without getting grinds in the coffee (grinder set on one notch up from percolator grind). Despite all the extra work and mess there was no improvement in the taste.

When I took it the filter out to clean it I saw the problem instantly, nearly all the coffee was bone-dry, the water never even touched it.

This does not work well at all and needs to be redesigned so the water is flowing over the grounds uniformly, not just down the center.

Several months after enjoying using my Keurig K55 brewer I decided to switch out the regular k cup holder and use the My K Cup instead.  I love k cups but I felt like I was constantly ordering them and that it would be cheaper to brew my own coffee grounds using the My Kup option. I was concerned about keeping the k cup holder needle around so I threw it away to avoid anyone accidently rooting around in the cabinets, reaching inside the box and stabbing themselves with it.  After about a week I realized I had made a huge mistake. Not only does the My Kcup brew weak coffee with coffee grounds mixed in. It also constantly drips water for several minutes after brewing. I end up having to put a washcloth down to absorb the moisture.  I researched and found out Keurig does not make replacement parts, so I've had to order an entire new brewer.  Don't make the same mistake I did of throwing out the needle.

I ordered two of these to replace a couple of older ones because the lids cracked in half (see photo). I've had four or five of these lids break along the left side, up to the red disc. Happens every time after a few months of use. Anyway, I haven't had the new ones long enough to see if they too will break, but I'm not a fan of the redesign. The new design has a wire basket with a lid, like the old one, but the basket then goes inside a plastic shell with a single hole in the bottom. So preparing one for use requires two steps instead of one, and cleaning is a pain. The old basket had a "handle" that I used to rap on the edge of a bowl to shake the grounds loose (I save my grounds for gardening). The new basket lacks the handle and is generally sort of flimsy, making it difficult to empty.
Also, the new design allows you to make either a cup or a carafe. Okay, not a bad idea, except that now you have to go through another menu, in which you must select either a picture of a carafe or a number, 1-6; then you get to another screen where you can select the size. There's really no explanation of what the numbers mean (I know, it's probably in the Keurig manual somewhere) so we just guess and then see what we get.
The whole thing is annoying. Amazon is famous for reducing transactional friction; it's disappointing when a company goes out of its way to increase friction.

In my opinion, the Old version of the Keurig My K-Cup is better than the New. In a cost saving move Keurig decided to manufacture one, modular, My K-Cup for both the Classic and Plus Series brewer, instead one for each. It works well for the Plus Series, but is poorly designed for the Classic series.

As you can see from the picture, the K-Cup Holder Assembly (left) and the "Old" version of the My K-Cup (center) are nearly an inch longer than the New version of the My K-Cup (right). As a result, over a period of time residue from the brewing process accumulates inside Keurig itself (instead of going into the coffee cup) and in turn, adversely effects the flavor of the coffee going forward. Yes, it can be cleaned by running coffee maker cleaner through the Keurig, but it with a little better design the problem could have been avoided. Hopefully, Keurig can get it right next time.
